expectation: NKG2A is a membrane marker on NK cells (CD56bright, immature CD56dim) and a subset of CD8 T cells. It should label a minority of scattered single cells with a membrane ring, perhaps more in tumour or lymphoid areas. It should not stain the whole tissue.
observed: A: broad yellow signal over the tissue body, following tissue density and outline, with dim edges and a faint stripe or tile pattern. B and C: diffuse haze filling stroma and lumen, with no discrete cells. D: a few ring-like outlines, but they sit in a generalised glow.
why: The signal is diffuse haze that follows tissue density, with no distinct sparse population of membrane-stained cells.
notes: Signal fills most of the tissue evenly and tracks density, not a cell type. B and C show haze without discrete stained cells. D has some ring shapes, but the background glow is as bright, so this is not a specific stain.
